proposed_defaults.match_seconds_limit_comment: User decision 2026-10-02/03: no time limit and no territory rule; a war ends only when one side holds every capital (the field is kept at 0 and unused).

economy.logistics_2_2_comment: 2.2 wave 2 (strategy, docs/BALANCE_LAB.md 2026-10-10 supply): 2.1/wave-1 30 + 80 × L share kept every stock 95–100 % full; 6 + 30 × L (≈ 105/min at the usual 15 % share, × army_scale) lets offensives drain their front towns while quiet fronts stay supplied.

territory.comment: User decision 2026-10-02: income and production grow with held settlements; values are per army_scale=1 and get multiplied by army_scale.
territory.income_comment: Balance lab 2026-10-03 (docs/BALANCE_LAB.md §5): territory income ×0.45 so late-game income stays near the loss rate instead of piling up at the population cap.
territory.income_2_2_comment: 2.2 (V22_SPEC §5, lead): settlement base output halved (2.1: village 4.5|1.8, town 13.5|18, city 22.5|42.75, point 6.75|5.4); economic buildings (econ section) earn the rest back.
territory.slots_comment: 2.2 (V22_SPEC §4): every place has its own queue; its slots = round(value × army_scale) (capital all facilities, city barracks + vehicle + support, town barracks only).
territory.pop_cap_comment: 1.1: the population cap is territory-driven. Capital base = capital_pop_share × population_cap; every held settlement adds pop_per_place × army_scale; ceiling = pop_cap_max_multiplier × population_cap. A side that owns most of the map can field a decisively larger army than the last defender, which is what ends a war.

victory.resolve_comment: User decision 2026-10-02: no campaign-resolve system; a faction is defeated only when its capital (HQ) is captured. Resolve fields below are kept for a possible optional mode.
victory.siege_blocks_production_comment: A capital with enemy combat troops inside this radius cannot roll out new units: a besieged capital can be taken instead of refilling its own capture ring forever.

logistics.comment: 2.2 supply rebuild (V22_SPEC §3). Stocks are cargo units (refilling 1.0 ammo costs a unit's supply_demand); values marked _k are per army_scale = 1 and multiplied by army_scale. Every owned capital / city / town holds a stock; logistics L (economy) fill them (towns lose part with distance from the capital, territory.depot_efficiency_*); convoys load from stocks; units near a stock draw from it at a gradual rate; a lost town loses its stock.
logistics.ammo_cost_comment: The one endurance lever: every weapon's ammo_cost × 2.5, so a full load lasts 40 % of 2.1.
logistics.stock_cap_comment: 2.2 wave 2: was 60 / 30 / 16 (stocks held 30+ minutes of consumption); a depot building (+14) now matters.
logistics.rearm_comment: Share of a full load a unit receives per second at a stock or a truck (40 s empty to full), before crowding.
logistics.crowd_comment: Units drawing at one stock / truck beyond crowd_free each get 1 / (1 + crowd_penalty × (n − crowd_free)) of the rate.
logistics.convoy_area_comment: Total cargo all trucks may hand over per second inside one 200 m cell (many trucks in one spot do not stack).
logistics.truck_fix_comment: 3.0 ammo-starved herd fix (docs/DEBUG_LAB.md): a loaded truck stops and hands over where it meets own units below truck_meet_below away from a stock; a threatened loaded truck falls back truck_fallback_m and hands over there instead of driving back to the depot full; an unloading truck waits truck_unload_wait_s for takers (was 12 s); a rearming unit walks to a loaded convoy within truck_meet_seek_m (and nearer than its stock) instead of back to a far stock. 0 switches meet / fallback / meet-seek off (A/B).
logistics.supply_round_comment: 2.2 supply round (docs/BALANCE_LAB.md 2026-10-10): rearming is a pause in the fight. A unit that fired in the last draw_contact_seconds draws only inside the settlement (its defenders) and takes nothing from a truck; trucks hand over within 80 m (units come to them), carry 25 and hand over 4 per second (area cap 0.6 k); rearm 0.012 of a load per second (≈ 80 s empty to full), walk to rearm below 0.08, back to the fight at 0.45. Was: draw 260/170/130 m, rearm 0.025, area 1.2, rearm 0.12 → 0.6, truck 40 / 8 / 190 m, seek 450 m.
logistics.fill_comment: 2.2 wave 2: a place refills at most place_fill_burst × its cap share of the logistics flow (a drained front town no longer takes the whole flow); the steward asks for more logistics while the stocks are below steward_stock_target of their caps.
logistics.contested_comment: A contested place pauses its queue; contested this long (or lost) its orders are refunded at economy.cancel_started_refund_ratio.

econ.comment: 2.2 economic buildings (V22_SPEC §5). Built with P/M at owned towns / cities (slots by kind), take build_seconds, have HP, are damaged by shellfire and demolished by raiders / engineers / attack-moving troops. A captured town keeps its buildings at most captured_hp_ratio of max HP; ruins can be rebuilt at rebuild_cost_ratio. Outputs (_k) are per army_scale = 1 and multiplied by army_scale × army_scale_income_factor (like territory income); output scales with HP.

econ_zones.comment: 3.0 engineer-built economic zones (经济区, V30_SPEC §7; econZones.ts). Built anywhere on own / neutral ground away from towns by an engineer job; level 1 → 2 → 3 by further jobs + cost. Output (_k: per army_scale 1, × army_scale × army_scale_income_factor, × HP share) is halved without a road link to an own town; a beaten side (capital_defence.min_held_share) gets beaten_output of it (lab: zones far behind the front kept losers alive). Raidable like economic buildings (shellfire, demolition), captured with the ground (HP capped at captured_hp_ratio), ruins rebuilt at rebuild_cost_ratio. enabled=false for the lab.

capital_defence.comment: 3.0 absolute defence perimeter (绝对国防圈, V23_SPEC §1.3 / V30_SPEC §8; capitalDefence.ts): a free, permanent ring of `strongpoints` bunker-hard strongpoints at radius_m around every capital, each with a fixed MG crew (crew_unit), plus a fixed artillery position (artillery_unit) behind the capital. Small arms cannot break the concrete (it must be stormed by armour or heavy guns); engineers repair it; a dead crew is replaced while its strongpoint stands and the enemy is not close. observation: in fog mode the capital sees every hostile within radius_m (shown on the minimap). A faction holding less than min_held_share of the mean settlements of the living factions (a beaten side, not a backdoor victim) no longer replaces crews or repairs the ring, so wars stay endable. enabled flags are for the lab.

defensive.comment: 2.0 defensive buildings (user: 工兵可以建设筑垒区域、炮楼、堡垒，需要步兵/侦察等单位进入驻防，不占人口). Built by engineers (structures.ts); costs are per building and NOT × army_scale (like unit costs). Buildings cost no population and squads inside them do not count against the population cap. A fortified zone (筑垒地域) is a planned layout of trenches + pillboxes + a bunker along a line, not a building of its own.
defensive.tiers_comment: 3.0 (V30_SPEC §8): works upgrade in place by engineers (worksTiers.ts): pillbox → bunker → fortress, trench → fortified trench (tier 1: hp × hp_mul, wider cover). AT emplacement = dug-in AT gun (accuracy and armour: absorb_share); 3.0 tuning (WP-T, docs/BALANCE_LAB.md 3.0 round): AT guns sit in bunkers and AT emplacements only (not fortresses), and a gun in concrete is light cover (cover 1, absorb 0.25-0.3): with cover 3 an equal-cost tank-led assault never broke a bunker or fortress line (0 %). Minefields: engineer-laid rectangles that slow hostile vehicles and blow them up by chance; engineers clear them slowly. Manned works see farther and spot for artillery. enabled=false switches the whole tier system off for the lab.

command.comment: 2.0 command hierarchy (user decision 2026-10-04): the supreme HQ (player or AI) gives each front one order (attack / defend / fortify / fall back / auto); a front commander unit executes it. Commanders are appointed, never produced.
command.compliance_comment: 3.0 directive compliance (V30_SPEC §6, compliance.ts): every HQ think each front computes compliance in [0,1] = base + proximity (near the capital) + temperament - risk (force ratio at its objective, own towns it would expose, ammunition). Below compliance_threshold it declines the directive and acts on its own; above it obeys after delay_s_per_km × km from the capital. A defend directive on the capital is never declined by fronts within home_recall_m. The same directive re-issued within insist_window_s (or the HUD Force toggle) is forced: obeyed at once by every front.
command.auto_resume_comment: 3.0.1 auto HQ (Faction.autoCommand, directive.chooseDirective): the doctrine AI picks the player's directive while no manual directive is in force; a manual directive other than advance pauses it for auto_resume_s after it was given.

fronts.comment: 3.0 fronts (V30_SPEC §5, frontTiers.ts): no hard cap (soft_max is a perf guard only). A front's command tier follows its combat units (tiers[].min_units, kept down to min_units - hysteresis_units): its batteries share one barrage target, its units get the morale (less morale loss) and accuracy bonus, supply_weight on the supply allocation and reinforce_weight on the reinforcement share. Fewer than stretched_units_per_100m units per 100 m of its stretch of the front line: stretched (accuracy / morale penalty). The theatre wants one front per units_per_front troops and per frontage_m_per_front of front line, opens a front for a cluster of >= tier-1 unattached troops (stray_m from their front) and merges a front under merge_below_units for merge_after_s.

infiltration.comment: 3.0 sparse fronts (V30_SPEC §11, zoc.ts / pickets.ts / infiltration.ts). Zone of control: an enemy within zoc_m of a front's line unit moves at zoc_speed_mul (refreshed every 0.5 s, held zoc_hold_s), is revealed to that faction, and up to engage_per_intruder line units chase it (engage_leash_m, engage_s); crossing the segment between two own line units closer than contact_gap_m is a line crossing and the front's reaction group intercepts (reaction_leash_m from its front). Pickets: a front spreads spare infantry (at most picket_max_share) along its stretch so no gap exceeds picket_gap_m x picket_tier_mul[tier], leaning picket_lean_m back; reaction group = reaction_share of its combat units (motorized first, then tanks; min/max units), reaction_back_m behind the line. Rear: a known enemy report_depth_m inside own ground (half the gap between the nearest hostile and the nearest own capital / held settlement; or near a standing report) and report_isolated_m from its own line units is an infiltrator; clusters (report_cluster_m) with >= report_min_value are reported (log + minimap blip), matched over report_match_m, forgotten after report_forget_s. Response: up to screen_max_places own towns / cities / economic towns / the capital within screen_radius_m get screen_squads_town / _city squads (picked within screen_pick_m, posted screen_post_m out toward the report, held screen_hold_s after it ends); the nearest free units within hunt_radius_m hunt it until hunt_ratio x its value (hunt_max_units, hunt_max_s); hunters + screens never exceed response_max_share of the faction's combat units.

doctrines.comment: 3.0 AI doctrines (V30_SPEC §1, sim/doctrines.ts, sim/doctrineai.ts, docs/DOCTRINES.md). Each AI supreme HQ has one: builder 优先发育, blitz 一波直捣黄龙, attrition 稳扎稳打, maneuver 寻机决战. The profile scales the existing AI levers (production mix and caps, investment appetite, occupation detachments, directive thresholds, damaged-unit retreat, raid cadence and targets, troops per front, compliance temperament, main-effort share, armour on the main front) and picks the doctrine offensive (late: convert a late lead; strike: one deep offensive on an enemy capital when the ratio is met, then re-arm; battle: hunt an isolated enemy front at attack_ratio). enabled=false = no doctrine effects (2.2 AI). The player's faction is never steered by its doctrine (it only colours the music in spectate).

transport.comment: 3.0 roads and railways (V30_SPEC §10, transport.ts / roadnet.ts / rail.ts / transportjobs.ts). enabled=false restores the 2.2 ground multipliers (road 1.05 foot / 1.35 vehicle, open 1) and switches rail and the engineer road/rail jobs off (lab A/B). On a road (or a town street) every class moves at on_road; off it at off_road[class], stacked with the forest / town / mud and grade modifiers. Class: vehicles tracked, crews towed, infantry infantry, overridden per unit by class_of.
transport.ford_comment: Extra navigation cost (×) of a ford cell: routes prefer bridges; movement speed on a ford is unchanged (mud).

rail.trucks_ride_comment: Lab 3.0 transport: trucks boarding trains made convoy trips 40 % fewer (waits at stations); supply moves by rail as the stock transfer between the two settlements of a held line instead.

upgrades.comment: 3.0 unit upgrades (V30_SPEC §9, docs/UPGRADES.md, src/sim/upgrades.ts). Bought with P/M by the supreme HQ, researched one at a time at the capital (seconds). Prices p_k / m_k are per army_scale x army_scale_income_factor = 1 (x2.5 at the default scale 10) and every owned item makes the next one `escalation` dearer. Armour, gun, attached guns and motorization reach existing units as a refit at a town rearm; the others at once.
